messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert - svc/runtime-prod reports 20% error rate on model-load RPCs, multiple nodes reporting OOM during model compile. Auto-escalation to oncall.
PagerDuty: Paging oncall (Ben K) for svc-runtime-prod - triggered by 5 distinct hosts within 3m.
Alex M: ack, I'm here. seeing a spike in `model_warmup_failures` and `cuda_driver_errors` from the compile stage.
Ben K: I'm taking lead. quick ask: can someone paste the latest stack traces from the node that died at 3625012200?
Priya S: pasting excerpt from /var/log/redwood/runtime.log on gpu-node-14:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] ERROR load: model=rw-v2-13b quant=fp16 compile-timeout
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] WARN cuda: driver err EV_DRV_XFER (nvlink timeout)
[2026-03-15T09:12:35Z] ERROR mem: allocation failed at 12.6GB during kv-cache alloc
[2026-03-15T09:12:36Z] FATAL warmup: deserialization failed: truncated payload
```
Priya S: the node also shows intermittent NVLINK resets in dmesg.
Lina R: confirming, we've got page-fault/GPU reset pattern. One of the hosts hit OOM while compiling kernels for the attention op.
Ben K: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) disable proactive warmup (stop prefetch/compile) so new containers lazy-load; 2) reroute traffic off affected AZ / node pool; 3) rollback to quantized fallback model (rw-v2-13b-q4) for high-throughput routes.
Alex M: +1. disabling warmup will reduce precompile pressure. doing `kubectl patch` now to scale warmup-deployment=0 in prod-canary.
Alex M: command: `kubectl -n prod patch deploy/model-warmup --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":0}}'`
Priya S: starting route change for affected customer groups (embedding-heavy) to fallback model. curl command: `curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/route/update -d '{"route":"/v1/embeddings","model":"rw-v2-13b-q4","reason":"runtime OOM/compile failures"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>"`
Ben K: please also mark on-call escalation in the incident channel and notify SRE rotation. Lina, can you start a rolling drain of gpu-node-14,15,16? prefer drain -> restart GPU driver -> uncordon.
Lina R: draining node list now: `for n in 14 15 16; do kubectl drain gpu-node-$n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; ssh gpu-node-$n 'sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver'; kubectl uncordon gpu-node-$n; done`
IncidentBot: Note: automated fallback applied to 7 routes. Telemetry shows success rate improving for canary traffic.
Ben K: observed a compile-timeout rate drop from 18% to 3% in the next 5m after warmup off + fallback routing. good.
Priya S: customer impact assessment in progress. early summary: a subset of Dedicated customers using large seq-length embeddings saw increases in 5xx and timeouts between 09:08-09:25 UTC. we're blocking further warmups to avoid stampede.
Alex M: who's owning postmortem? we should capture NVLINK resets + deserialization truncation root cause.
Ben K: I'll own incident writeup and postmortem. action items: collect kernel logs from affected hosts, upload model artifact checksums, validate artifact integrity (deserialization truncation could be artifact truncation during push).
Lina R: done on node drains, restarted drivers, nodes are back in rotation. memory pressure reduced.
Priya S: quick note to Support: "We're mitigating a model-load/compile issue causing transient 5xx for some customers. fallback applied to embeddings routes. No long-term data loss. We'll update in 30m."
Ben K: follow-up mitigation: add a soft rate limit on concurrent warmups per node: set `WARMUP_MAX_CONCURRENT=2` in runtime config and roll config to prod to prevent future compile storms.
Alex M: pushed config change to canary: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime --env=WARMUP_MAX_CONCURRENT=2 -n prod-canary`
IncidentBot: Incident status -> Mitigated. Continued monitoring.
Priya S: monitoring shows error rate back to baseline for most routes; two customers (AcmeCorp, NimbusHealth) still showing elevated latency for embeddings. Eng-sre to coordinate with account teams for targeted retries.
Ben K: timeline + summary to be posted in 2 hours. tagging @pagerduty for follow up. closing active page. :white_check_mark:
Lina R: small follow-up - we should add NVLINK error counters to the node exporter dashboard and alert at lower thresholds.
Ben K: agreed, adding an RFC for better HW heuristics and fallback to quantized variants when compile queue depth > 10.
IncidentBot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 3625012980.
